authoring_notes.structure: 95 chapters across 10 phases ordered by the training pipeline: foundations → pretraining (scaling and data) → mid-training and context extension → synthetic data → SFT and distillation → preference optimization → RL including agentic RL → evaluation → infrastructure → capstone. 36 chapters are new and 59 are existing ids (ch-01..ch-59). Some existing chapters move to the phase where their stage occurs (ch-32 to mid-training, ch-15 and ch-41 to preference, ch-16 to RL).
authoring_notes.learning_order: Array order is the learning order. A reader starting the course reads the chapters array from ch-00 to ch-59 in sequence; every dep of a chapter appears earlier in the array. Suffix ids do not follow numeric order across phases (for example ch-32..ch-32f precede ch-18, and ch-15 and ch-41 precede ch-37), so the array, not the id number, defines the order.
authoring_notes.learner_resume_path: This learner's path differs from array order in one way: the SFT phase is read before the unstudied pretraining and mid-training phases, because ch-24 and ch-30 are in progress. Studied and read-only chapters (ch-18..ch-23, ch-25..ch-29) count as satisfied dependencies; their errata are read when a later chapter links to them and need no new verdict. Steps: (1) Finish ch-24 (qa.md Q1-Q16 exist; read the errata additions, then Discuss). (2) ch-00, the measurement contract (dep of ch-29e and ch-47). (3) ch-04, packing, masking and chat templates (dep of ch-30). (4) SFT phase: ch-29e → ch-30 (resume; qa.md Q1 exists) → ch-30a → ch-30b → ch-30c → ch-31 → ch-31a → ch-33 → ch-34 → ch-35 → ch-35a → ch-36 (lab). None of these depends on an unstudied pretraining or mid-training chapter. (5) Pretraining: ch-01 → ch-02 → ch-03 → ch-08a → ch-08b → ch-09 → ch-10 → ch-10a → ch-11 → ch-12 → ch-12a → ch-13 → ch-13a → ch-14 → ch-14a. Foundations ch-05..ch-08 and the ch-17 lab can be deferred: no chapter outside that group depends on them. (6) Mid-training: ch-32 → ch-32a → ch-32b → ch-32c → ch-32d → ch-32e (ch-32f lab optional here). (7) Synthetic additions that need mid-training: ch-29a → ch-29b → ch-29c → ch-29d. (8) Continue in array order from ch-15: preference (ch-15..ch-42a), RL (ch-40..ch-46a), evaluation (ch-47..ch-53), infrastructure (ch-54..ch-58), capstone (ch-58a, ch-59), then any deferred foundations chapters and labs.
authoring_notes.course_goal: Every chapter serves the standing goal set on 2026-09-14: building a generally capable model. Every content chapter has a Recipe section and a Generalization lens section (style-guide §4-§5); chapters whose stage produces or uses negative signals have a Negative samples and negative feedback section (style-guide §6).
authoring_notes.id_scheme: Existing ids ch-01..ch-59 keep their topics and directories. New chapters take a suffix of the chapter they follow in the array (ch-08a, ch-32b, ...); ch-00 opens the course. Merged-away draft ids (ch-35b, ch-42b, ch-53a, ch-54a) are not used and must not be created as directories.
authoring_notes.merges_and_drops: From the 99-chapter draft: ch-42b merged into ch-45a (same question for preference and RL settings); ch-54a merged into ch-54 (same rollout-infrastructure question); ch-35b dropped with its SFT ledger moved to ch-34, its distillation-SFT ledger to ch-35a, and scale transfer to ch-58a; ch-53a dropped because ch-05, ch-06, ch-11, ch-14a, and ch-32e cover mixture loaders, schedules, in-loop evaluation, and released configs. ch-32f was kept because no other chapter runs a context-extension experiment.
authoring_notes.core_question_rule: Each chapter carries one core_question. Concepts that answer a different chapter's core question appear only as a pointer to that chapter (for example ReST-EM is taught in ch-31 and referenced from ch-45; judge bias measurement is taught in ch-49 and referenced from ch-42).
authoring_notes.record_preservation: Studied chapters keep their ids, topics, verdict.json and qa.md. Their read.md receives an append-only errata list; qa.md receives new correction entries without editing earlier ones. deps of studied chapters are re-pointed to pipeline prerequisites; this does not change their verdicts.
authoring_notes.change_labels: unchanged: no edits; revised: topic and structure kept, factual corrections and added sections (studied chapters use append-only errata); rewritten: topic kept, content rebuilt from primary sources; rescoped: topic boundary changed; new: chapter did not exist.
authoring_notes.chapter_types: content: one Read → Discuss cycle with 5-8 concepts and one core question. lab: produces a measured artifact; every lab reports a before/after generality measurement. capstone: exactly one (ch-59).
authoring_notes.recipe_chapters: Every content chapter has a Recipe section. Side-by-side recipe comparisons: ch-14a (pretraining), ch-32e (mid-training and context extension), ch-34 (SFT-stage ledger across case-study models), ch-35a (distillation-SFT student settings), ch-45a (preference optimization and RL), ch-45d (agentic), ch-58a (end to end). Canonical values live in source-card Recipe ledgers (style-guide §5.1).

New cards must be written and insights.md rows added before a chapter is authored (CLAUDE.md raw-source rules). Non-paper sources carry reliability labels: official, practitioner-evidence, anecdotal.

CP) from ch-05/ch-54; on-policy-distillation (ch-04 mechanism, ch-05 economics, ch-06 GKD recipes) from ch-35/ch-35a/ch-57; llm-arch (ch-06 positional encoding, ch-10 scaling laws, ch-16 long context) from ch-08a/ch-32b.
authoring_notes.authoring_preconditions: Before authoring rewritten or new chapters: correct the library cards named in each change_note; rewrite longmit, prolong, long-context-llama3, qwen-long-context-synth and longchat cards; merge the enrich_existing extracts into deepseek-r1, smollm-3, llama-2, ruler, tulu-3, longmit, minimax-01, openr1, phi-4, and qwen-3 before citing those facts; add cards for MiniMax-M1 and Feng et al. (Beyond Model Collapse); do not cite the no-primary-source cards faithful-synth-eval, minibatch-sharing-rl, packed-vs-unpacked-ablation; run a dedicated fact-refutation pass per chapter (outline-verification memory).
authoring_notes.per_chapter_format: Each read.md quotes real code/equations from the raw-data library and extracts the chapter's core insight + guideline. Chapters may emit companion HTML files under ch-XX/figures/ or ch-XX/animations/ for architecture diagrams, parameter explorers, or step-by-step animations (see CLAUDE.md 'Chapter authoring — HTML visualizations').
authoring_notes.lab_paths: Every lab chapter offers two paths. Full-budget path: multi-GPU, 1B–3B model, end-to-end run. Resource-constrained path: single-node or single-GPU, 125M–1B model, partial reproduction with replayed logs or precomputed rollouts where feasible. The memo/artifact requirement is the same in both paths — only the training scale differs.
authoring_notes.rl_vs_eval_boundary: RL track covers reward and judge topics as they are used during optimization — RM training, reward hacking, judge-driven preference loops, Constitutional AI, RLAIF. Eval track covers judges as measurement instruments — calibration, position/verbosity/self-enhancement bias audits, contamination workflow, slice analysis, go/no-go memos. If a topic is about producing a signal for training, it belongs in RL; if it is about auditing or comparing checkpoints, it belongs in Eval.

tracks.title: Foundations: Measuring General Capability and Training Mechanics
tracks.purpose: Define general capability operationally and teach the optimizer, precision, schedule, packing, distributed, checkpointing, and failure-detection choices whose effects every later stage depends on.

tracks.title: Pretraining: Scaling Laws and Pretraining Data
tracks.purpose: Explain why next-token pretraining produces broad ability and how compute allocation, data composition, filtering, deduplication, memorization, mixing, multilingual coverage, and recipe settings widen or narrow it.

tracks.title: Mid-Training, Continued Pretraining, and Context Extension
tracks.purpose: Teach the stages between pretraining and post-training: annealing data, continued pretraining without forgetting, context-length extension with short-context regression gates, effective-length evaluation, agentic mid-training, and their recipes.

tracks.title: Synthetic Data Generation and Verification
tracks.purpose: Teach the generate-filter-verify-select-mix pattern across data types, including reasoning traces, conversations, tools, long documents, long conversations, agentic environments, user simulators, and failed trajectories.

tracks.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning and Distillation
tracks.purpose: Teach instruction-tuning generalization, SFT design choices, forgetting, skill mixtures, merging, supervised use of negatives, case-study SFT recipes side by side, and how labs place and build distillation data.

tracks.title: Preference Data, Reward Models, and Preference Optimization
tracks.purpose: Teach human preference data, reward modeling, policy-gradient and KL-controlled RLHF foundations, SFT-versus-RL generalization, DPO-family objectives with their negative gradient, reward hacking, and broad behaviour change from narrow training.

tracks.title: Reinforcement Learning, Including Agentic RL
tracks.purpose: Teach group-baseline RL, prompt distributions, entropy and KL, negative gradients, verifiable and non-verifiable rewards, length and long-context RL, multi-domain RL, preference and RL recipes side by side, and multi-turn agentic RL with context management.

tracks.title: Evaluation of General Capability
tracks.purpose: Teach harness and suite design, benchmark-overfitting audits, contamination, judges, slices, statistics, agent evaluation, and safety evaluation as the measurement layer for every training stage.

tracks.title: Training and RL Infrastructure
tracks.purpose: Teach rollout and asynchronous RL infrastructure including agentic environments, and framework internals, with a focus on instrumentation that detects general-capability regression.

tracks.title: End-to-End Recipes and Capstone
tracks.purpose: Compare open end-to-end recipes and reproduce one stage with a generality gate.

chapters.title: What General Capability Means and How It Is Measured
chapters.core_question: What does "generally capable" mean operationally, and how is it measured without false generality claims?
concepts: Operational definition used by the whole course: performance on tasks and domains that were not targeted during training, reported as a capability profile rather than a single score

Capability coverage map for a general model: knowledge, reasoning and math, code, instruction following, long context, multilingual, tool use and agentic tasks, factuality and calibration, safety and over-refusal
Development suite versus held-out (unseen) suite: the Tülu 3 evaluation regime and why the gap between the two estimates overfitting to the development benchmarks
Base-model measurement: per-domain held-out perplexity (Paloma) and standardized formats (OLMES); why cloze and multiple-choice formulations give different rankings at small scale
Measurement error: seed variance, benchmark signal-to-noise, and prompt-format sensitivity (FormatSpread) as quantified sources of false generality claims
Narrowing signals that every later chapter reports: forgetting against the base model, pass@1 versus pass@k, output diversity, over-refusal, and contamination-inflated scores
Source types and reliability labels used in the course: peer-reviewed paper, official technical report, official blog or model card, released config or code, practitioner evidence, anecdotal report
chapters.change_note: Brief A (generality audit, first new chapter). Placed first so every later chapter reuses one measurement contract. In the learner resume path it is read right after finishing ch-24 and before the SFT phase.

chapters.title: Optimizers for LLM Training: AdamW, Update Size, and Retention of Prior Ability
chapters.core_question: Which optimizer settings determine how far an update moves the model, and how does that affect retained ability?
concepts: AdamW update rule and what decoupled weight decay changes relative to L2 regularization, with every symbol defined
Why Adam outperforms SGD on language data: heavy-tailed token-frequency imbalance and the learning of rare tokens (Kunstner et al. 2024)
Weight decay in single-epoch pretraining as a control on effective learning rate and final loss, contrasted with multi-epoch SFT where overfitting occurs
β₂ and ε choices reported by open model reports, each tied to a specific run and locus
Gradient clipping by global norm: the formula, where it sits relative to loss unscaling, and its interaction with RL reward spikes
Update size in fine-tuning: learning rate and step count as determinants of distance from the initial weights, with the forgetting evidence taught in ch-30a
Newer optimizers (Muon, Lion, Shampoo-family) judged by reported downstream breadth, not only by training loss
chapters.change_note: Topic kept. Audit found wrong claims (clip-before-unscale, muP/SGD, beta2 history, WD rationale); adds update-size-versus-forgetting section. classics/adam.md must be corrected first.

chapters.title: Numerical Precision, Determinism, and Train–Inference Mismatch
chapters.core_question: How do numerical formats and nondeterminism change training stability, evaluation scores, and RL log-probabilities?
concepts: fp32, fp16, bf16 and fp8 formats: exponent and mantissa bits, representable range, and which operations are kept in higher precision
Loss scaling for fp16 and why bf16 does not require it
Block-wise fp8 training as reported for DeepSeek-V3, and what its BF16 comparison ablations do and do not establish about downstream capability
Precision and tokens-per-parameter: Scaling Laws for Precision and the higher quantization cost of models trained at high tokens-per-parameter ratios
Numerical nondeterminism in evaluation: dtype, batch size, and GPU count move reasoning benchmark scores; batch-invariant inference as the remedy
Numerical sources of sampler–trainer log-probability mismatch (kernels, precision, batch composition), with the RL correction taught in ch-54
Instability symptoms (loss spikes, NaN, softmax overflow) and the checks that separate numerical causes from data causes
chapters.change_note: Topic kept but corrected (fp8 ranges, DeepSeek-V3 scheme, fp32 op rules). Brief suggested merging into ch-01/ch-03; design A keeps the id and adds evaluation reproducibility and RL mismatch instead of rescoping.

chapters.title: Learning-Rate Schedules, Batch Size, Initialization, and Normalization
chapters.core_question: How do learning-rate schedules, batch size, initialization, and normalization determine stable training and final capability?
concepts: Warmup, cosine, inverse-square-root, and warmup-stable-decay (WSD) schedules; most final-loss reduction in WSD occurs during the decay phase
The decay phase as the place where high-quality data is inserted (MiniCPM, OLMo 2 Dolmino, Llama 3 annealing), with a forward link to ch-32
Critical batch size and learning-rate scaling with batch size (linear versus square root), with measured critical-batch-size results
Initialization schemes (Xavier, Kaiming, GPT-2 residual scaling) and muP hyperparameter transfer as the reason small ablations predict large runs
LayerNorm versus RMSNorm, pre-norm versus post-norm, QK-norm, and the OLMo 2 normalization placement, each with the reported stability evidence
Learning rate for context-extension continued pretraining (ProLong, Kimi k1.5) as a pointer to ch-32b
Over-training and fine-tuning plasticity: evidence that checkpoints trained at high tokens-per-parameter ratios are harder to fine-tune
chapters.change_note: Structure kept; muP table, reordered-norm description, QK-norm adoption claims and worked failure case corrected. Adds batch-size scaling and the annealing-to-capability link.

chapters.title: Sequence Packing, Loss Masking, and Chat Templates
chapters.core_question: How do packing, loss masking, and chat templates change what the model is trained on and how it generalizes across formats?
concepts: Packing with variable-length attention (cu_seqlens), cross-document attention masking, and best-fit packing that avoids truncation
Position IDs under RoPE with a correct block-diagonal mask: when resets matter and when a constant offset leaves attention unchanged
Prompt-masked versus full-sequence loss as a generalization choice: instruction modelling (Shi et al. 2024) and prompt-loss weight results
Chat-template design (special tokens for turns, thinking, and tool calls) and the failure, which raises no error, when training and inference templates differ
Format and template overfitting: FormatSpread and Mind Your Format results, and template diversification during SFT
Intra-document causal masking and its reported effect on in-context and few-shot behaviour
Tokenizer and template co-design when adding reasoning or tool tokens after pretraining
chapters.change_note: Central masking guideline contradicted its cited paper and the NEFTune formula was wrong. Adds format overfitting and long-sequence document masking.

chapters.title: Distributed Training Choices That Change Batch Size, Sequence Length, and Tokens Seen
chapters.core_question: Which distributed-training choices change batch size, sequence length, tokens seen, and the realized data mixture?
concepts: Data, tensor, pipeline, expert, and context parallelism summarized as a reference; memory mechanics are linked to training-memory ch-07 rather than re-derived
Global batch in tokens, tokens per step, and throughput as the quantities that connect a parallelism layout to compute-optimal or over-trained allocation
Context and sequence parallelism for long sequences: ring attention, DeepSpeed Ulysses, and all-gather-KV CP as used in the Llama 3 long-context stage
How data sharding and sampling across data-parallel ranks and resumes realize or distort the intended data mixture
Expert parallelism and load balancing (DeepSeek-V3 auxiliary-loss-free balancing) with reported downstream evaluations
World-size arithmetic (TP x PP x CP x DP) for published runs, with the source locus for each factor
chapters.change_note: Condensed rather than rescoped: memory table, 1F1B diagram and DeepSeek-V3 layout were wrong; mechanics now point to the training-memory course (ch-06 kernels, ch-07 parallelism).

chapters.title: Checkpointing, In-Loop Evaluation, and Checkpoint Selection
chapters.core_question: How should checkpoints be saved, evaluated during training, and selected so that general capability is tracked?
concepts: Contents of a resumable checkpoint (weights, optimizer state, scheduler state, RNG, data-loader position) as a corrected checklist

In-loop measurement of generality: multi-domain held-out perplexity (Paloma subsets) and low-noise downstream evaluations with standardized formats, as configured in OLMo-core and nanotron training code
Benchmark signal-to-noise at ablation scale and which tasks can separate small-scale decisions (Signal and Noise, DataDecide)
Checkpoint averaging during annealing (Llama 3) and model merging during pretraining as evidence-backed selection tools
Early stopping for SFT on a held-out general suite rather than target validation loss: Tülu 3 epoch results and IFEval degradation
Per-domain and per-shard loss tracking to detect mixture drift or a data-loader desynchronization after resume that raises no error
chapters.change_note: Topic kept; checkpoint mechanics corrected (FSDP master weights, scaler, invented Karpathy rule); instrumentation reframed as in-training measurement of general capability.

chapters.title: Training Failure Modes: Numerical, Masking, and Capability-Level Failures
chapters.core_question: How are numerical, masking, and capability-level training failures detected and told apart?
concepts: Numerical failures (NaN and Inf from softmax overflow, log of zero in KL, zero division in advantage normalization) with a diagnostic order
Masking and packing correctness bugs: missing cu_seqlens, dense kernels on packed data, off-by-one label shifts, and the correct risk model for un-reset position IDs
Loss divergence, spike, and plateau: diagnostic trees that separate optimizer, data, and precision causes
Capability-level failures with their detectors: SFT overfitting from repeated epochs, catastrophic forgetting and alignment tax, contamination-inflated scores, template overfitting
RL-specific failures as loss of diversity: entropy collapse, reward hacking, and length exploitation, with pass@k and held-out suites as detectors
Regression suite per failure: which broad benchmark or held-out perplexity slice exposes each failure mode
chapters.change_note: Fabrications removed (OLMo 3 padding scare, skip-step stack, Karpathy quote). Distributed-hang operations move to the training-memory course; capability-level failure modes added.

chapters.title: Lab: Minimal Trainer with a Target-versus-General Capability Measurement
chapters.core_question: Does a minimal SFT run improve its target task while retaining general capability, measured with valid tests?
concepts: Read one small trainer end to end against the current TRL release, verifying every symbol in source
Replace invalid gates with valid tests: packed versus unpacked logit equivalence, decoded inspection of labels not equal to -100, step-1 loss compared with the base model's held-out loss
Run a small SFT with FSDP and mixed precision; evaluate base and SFT checkpoints on a broad suite (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, IFEval, Paloma subset) next to the target task
Ablate overfitting factors with seeds or confidence intervals: epochs 1/2/3, learning rate, response-only versus instruction-modelling loss, one versus diversified templates
Deliverable: memo reporting target gain against general regression, with a template-robustness evaluation under two prompt formats
Resource-constrained path: 125M-500M model on one GPU; the before/after generality table is still required
chapters.change_note: Two of six gates were impossible for a correct run and the TRL mapping was stale. Deliverable becomes a measured target-versus-general trade-off.

chapters.title: Scaling Laws and Compute Allocation: From Pretraining Loss to Downstream Capability
chapters.core_question: How should a fixed compute budget be split between parameters and tokens, and how well does pretraining loss predict downstream capability?
concepts: Kaplan and Chinchilla power laws for loss as a function of parameters and tokens, with every fitted symbol defined and the reason the two allocations disagree (Porian et al. resolution)
Compute-optimal tokens per parameter versus deliberate over-training for inference cost (Beyond Chinchilla-Optimal; Llama 3 8B; SmolLM2)
Predicting downstream accuracy from loss: over-training and downstream scaling (Gadre et al.), Llama 3's two-step NLL-to-accuracy fit, and task scaling with model ladders
Where downstream prediction fails: scaling laws unreliable for downstream tasks, and why frontier downstream capability has been hard to predict
Data-constrained scaling as the link to ch-14: repeated tokens versus unique tokens
Plasticity cost of over-training: evidence that base models trained at high tokens-per-parameter ratios lose more under fine-tuning
Worked allocation exercise: a fixed FLOP budget split into model size and tokens under three objectives (loss, inference cost, fine-tunability)
chapters.change_note: Brief A: no scaling-law chapter existed. Placed at the start of the pretraining phase instead of the foundations track so that ch-02/ch-05 need not be rescoped.

chapters.title: Why Next-Token Pretraining Produces General Ability: In-Context Learning, Emergence, and Predictability
chapters.core_question: Why does next-token prediction on broad text produce abilities that were not targeted, and when are those abilities predictable?
concepts: Language modeling as unsupervised multitask learning (GPT-2) and few-shot in-context learning (GPT-3), stated with the reported task counts and scores
Data distributional properties that produce in-context learning: burstiness and long-tail class structure (Chan et al. 2022)
Induction heads as a mechanistic account of in-context copying and its reported phase change during training
Emergent abilities versus metric artifacts: discontinuous metrics, continuous metrics, and the loss-threshold view of emergence
Same pretraining loss, different downstream results: implicit bias of the optimizer and architecture
Embers of autoregression: output-probability sensitivity as a predictor of where a pretrained model generalizes poorly
Implication for data decisions: breadth of pretraining distribution versus benchmark-shaped data as determinants of transfer
chapters.change_note: Brief A: no chapter explained the mechanism of generality. Recipe section is short (context length, data diversity settings of GPT-2/GPT-3) and states which settings are not reported.

chapters.title: Pretraining Data Composition and Capability Coverage
chapters.core_question: Which pretraining data sources supply which capabilities, and how does composition change downstream breadth?
concepts: Source types and the capabilities they supply: web, code, books, academic text, Wikipedia, math, multilingual text, with the Pile cross-domain bits-per-byte comparison
Measured effects of composition on a broad downstream suite: data age, domain removal, and quality or toxicity filters (A Pretrainer's Guide to Training Data)
Llama 3 final mixture (general knowledge, math and reasoning, code, multilingual shares) set by scaling-law experiments and a knowledge classifier that downsamples over-represented web categories
Code in pretraining: controlled evidence on transfer to reasoning and non-code tasks
Open corpora and what each discloses (The Pile, Dolma, FineWeb, DCLM, Nemotron-CC) compared with closed reports
Opt-outs and consent restrictions as measured reductions in coverage (Consent in Crisis), replacing the unsourced governance section
chapters.change_note: Reframed from disclosure politics to composition and capability coverage; central-table numbers (Pile weights, Llama 3 mix, FineWeb classifier) were wrong.

chapters.title: Heuristic Curation Pipelines: CCNet, C4, Dolma, FineWeb
chapters.core_question: What do heuristic curation pipelines remove, and how do their filters change domain and dialect coverage?
concepts: CCNet stage order (deduplication, language identification, perplexity-based quality bucketing) as stated in the paper
C4 heuristic filters and line-level deduplication, with the reported side effects on dialect and topic coverage
Dolma per-source pipelines and the filter ablations actually reported in the paper
FineWeb pipeline: extraction, heuristic filters, per-snapshot MinHash settings, and the reason given for per-snapshot rather than global deduplication
Filters as distribution selectors: which topic clusters and domains each filter removes, measured with Paloma domain fit
How to read a new pipeline: filter order, thresholds, ablation design, and evaluation suite used to select each threshold
chapters.change_note: Scope kept to classical pipelines; model-based filtering moves to new ch-10a. CCNet ordering, FineWeb MinHash settings, PII handling and the Dolma ablation were wrong or invented.

chapters.title: Model-Based Quality Filtering and Benchmark-Targeted Data Selection
chapters.core_question: When does model-based quality filtering broaden capability, and when does it select benchmark-shaped data that narrows it?
concepts: Classifier-based quality filtering: FineWeb-Edu annotation, classifier, and threshold choice with its MMLU/ARC gain and HellaSwag loss
DCLM fastText filter with instruction-shaped positives (OpenHermes-2.5, ELI5) and DCLM Core versus Extended suites as a breadth check
Nemotron-CC: ensembles of classifiers and rephrasing to recover unique tokens after aggressive filtering, and the quality-versus-quantity constraint at 15T-token horizons
QuRating, WebOrganizer topic and format domains, perplexity-correlation selection, and datamodel-based selection as alternative selection objectives
Benchmark-targeted selection: classifier positives that resemble evaluation content, training on the test task, and detection of targeted gains with held-out tasks
Small-scale data decisions and whether their rankings transfer to larger models (DataDecide)
Language and dialect bias introduced by quality classifiers
chapters.change_note: Brief A. The negative-feedback section covers negatives in the sense of negative marginal value (samples removed by a filter) and classifier negative examples.

chapters.title: Tokenizers, Data Provenance, and PII Removal
chapters.core_question: How do tokenizer, provenance, and PII-removal choices affect coverage, memorization, and reproducibility of a corpus?
concepts: Tokenizer training (BPE, Unigram) and vocabulary size, with vocabulary scaling laws relating optimal vocabulary to model size
Tokenizer effects on breadth: cross-lingual fertility disparity, digit tokenization and arithmetic, and under-trained tokens
Extending a tokenizer for new languages or special tokens with continued pretraining and a retention measurement
Training-data provenance tools that separate memorization from generalization: infini-gram, WIMBD, OLMoTrace-style search
PII and secret removal as a pipeline stage, connected to memorization and extraction evidence
Shard and streaming formats reduced to one reference section: how configured mixture weights become token shares and how sampler state preserves them on resume
chapters.change_note: Topic kept (tokenizers, lineage, PII) with operations material condensed; nearly every number in the old chapter was invented or misattributed.

chapters.title: Deduplication: Exact, Near-Duplicate, and Semantic
chapters.core_question: How do exact, near-duplicate, and semantic deduplication change repetition, diversity, and downstream quality?
concepts: Lee et al. 2021 deduplication results with the parameters stated correctly, and the corrected card values
MinHash with LSH: Jaccard estimation, number of permutations, band and row parameters, and collision probability with a worked example
Suffix-array exact substring deduplication and when span-level deduplication matters
Semantic deduplication and diversification (SemDeDup, D4) and D4's result that diversified selection with repetition can beat fresh random data
Repetition structure and generalization: repeating a small subset many times degrades performance beyond its token share (Hernandez et al. 2022)
Global versus per-snapshot deduplication as a quality and coverage trade-off (FineWeb versus Llama 3)

chapters.title: Memorization, Knowledge Acquisition, and Generalization During Pretraining
chapters.core_question: Under what data conditions does pretraining store knowledge in an extractable form rather than as memorized strings?
concepts: Memorization scaling with duplication count, model size, and context length (Quantifying Memorization; How much do LMs memorize)
Memorization without overfitting: training dynamics in which memorization precedes and coexists with generalization
Knowledge storage and extraction: facts become extractable only when training data contains diverse rephrasings (Physics of LM 3.1) and manipulation limits (3.2)
The reversal curse as a limit on bidirectional knowledge from one-directional training text
Factual knowledge acquisition and forgetting dynamics during pretraining, and long-tail knowledge frequency thresholds
Influence functions as a tool for tracing which training documents drive a generalization
Consequences for data design: rephrasing and augmentation of rare facts versus repetition of the same string
chapters.change_note: Brief A. Takes over the knowledge-retention half of ch-14, which had no supporting evidence.

chapters.title: Domain Mixing: DoReMi, Mixture Laws, and Validation Across Scale
chapters.core_question: How should domain mixture weights be chosen and validated so that they transfer across model scale and training stages?
concepts: DoReMi as a worst-group robustness objective: proxy model, reference model, exponentiated-gradient update, and the reported result on all 22 Pile domains
Mixture laws and regression-based mixing: Data Mixing Laws, RegMix, and Aioli's finding that many methods do not consistently beat stratified sampling
